fullPassage: One fundamental implication derived from the existence of human action is the uncertainty of the future. This must be true because the contrary would completely deny the possibility of action. If man knew future events completely, he would never act, since no act of his could change the situation. Thus the fact of action signifies that the future is uncertain to the actors. This uncertainty about future events stems from two basic sources: the unpredictability of human acts of choice, and insufficient knowledge about natural phenomena. Man does not know enough about natural phenomena to predict all their future developments, and he cannot know the content of future human choices. All human choices are continually changing as a result of changing valuations and changing ideas about the most appropriate means of arriving at ends. This does not mean, of course, that people do not try their best to estimate future developments. Indeed, any actor, when employing means, estimates that he will thus arrive at his desired goal. But he never has certain knowledge of the future. All his actions are of necessity speculations based on his judgment of the course of future events. The omnipresence of uncertainty introduces the ever-present possibility of error in human action. The actor may find, after he has completed his action, that the means have been inappropriate to the attainment of his end.

det.korean: 근본적인(fundamental), 불충분한(insufficient), 적절한(appropriate)이 문맥상 적절합니다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① fundamental — insufficient — appropriate: 인간 행동의 '근본적' 함의, 자연현상에 대한 '불충분한' 지식, 목적에 도달하는 가장 '적절한' 수단.
❌ ② superficial — insufficient — appropriate: (A) '피상적인'이 아니라 '근본적인' 함의.
❌ ③ fundamental — excessive — appropriate: (B) '과도한' 지식이 아니라 '불충분한' 지식.
❌ ④ fundamental — insufficient — irrelevant: (C) '무관한' 수단이 아니라 '적절한' 수단.
det.tip: fundamental(근본적인) ↔ superficial(피상적인), insufficient(불충분한) ↔ excessive(과도한), appropriate(적절한) ↔ irrelevant(무관한)

questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 불확실성(uncertainty), 예측불가능성(unpredictability), 확실한(certain)이 문맥상 적절합니다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① certainty — unpredictability — certain: (A) '확실성'이 아니라 '불확실성'.
❌ ② uncertainty — predictability — certain: (B) '예측가능성'이 아니라 '예측불가능성'.
❌ ③ uncertainty — unpredictability — uncertain: (C) 'never has uncertain knowledge'는 이중부정으로 의미 부적절. 원문은 'never has certain knowledge'.
✅ ④ uncertainty — unpredictability — certain: 미래의 '불확실성', 선택의 '예측불가능성', 하지만 '확실한' 지식은 없다(never has certain knowledge).

det.korean: 부정하다(deny), 계속해서(continually), 추측(speculations)이 문맥상 적절합니다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① deny — continually — speculations: 미래를 알면 행동 가능성을 '부정'하고, 선택은 '계속해서' 변하며, 행동은 '추측'에 기반.

❌ ③ deny — rarely — speculations: (B) 선택이 '드물게'가 아니라 '계속해서' 변함.
❌ ② deny — continually — certainties: (C) '확실성'이 아니라 '추측'에 기반.
det.tip: deny(부정하다) ↔ confirm(확인하다), continually(계속해서) ↔ rarely(드물게), speculations(추측) ↔ certainties(확실성)

questions.passage: One fundamental implication derived from the existence of human action is the uncertainty of the future. This must be true because the contrary would completely deny the possibility of action. If man knew future events completely, he would never act, since no act of his could change the situation. Thus the fact of action signifies that the future is uncertain to the actors. This uncertainty about future events stems from two basic sources: the unpredictability of human acts of choice, and <u>insufficient</u> knowledge about natural phenomena. Man does not know enough about natural phenomena to predict all their future developments, and he cannot know the content of future human choices. All human choices are continually changing as a result of changing valuations and changing ideas about the most appropriate means of arriving at ends. This does not mean, of course, that people do not try their best to estimate future developments. Indeed, any actor, when employing means, estimates that he will thus arrive at his desired goal. But he never has certain knowledge of the future. All his actions are of necessity speculations based on his judgment of the course of future events. The omnipresence of uncertainty introduces the ever-present possibility of error in human action. The actor may find, after he has completed his action, that the means have been inappropriate to the attainment of his end.

det.korean: insufficient (불충분한) ↔ adequate (충분한)

❌ ② lacking: '부족한'은 insufficient과 동의어.
❌ ③ partial: '부분적인'은 불충분과 유사.
❌ ④ limited: '제한된'은 insufficient과 유사한 뉘앙스.
